theme: Housing affordability and STR-housing studies data: rent-burden, vacancy, STR share of housing stock by tract
queries_run: gh search repos "short term rental housing stock share" --sort stars
gh search repos "rental vacancy rate dataset" --sort stars
gh search repos "airbnb housing affordability" --sort stars
gh search repos "rent burden dataset" --sort stars
gh search repos "airbnb rent effect" --sort stars
gh search repos "HUD fair market rent" --sort stars
gh search repos "short-term rental impact housing prices" --sort stars
WebSearch site:github.com short-term rental housing stock share census tract dataset (blocked, session web-search budget exhausted)
WebSearch site:github.com AirDNA sample data repository (blocked, session web-search budget exhausted)

candidates.name: Zoning-and-Rent-Burdens
candidates.what_it_holds: Python/R pipeline combining Census ACS data (via API), 2021 TIGER/Line shapefiles (CBSA + state boundaries), HUD Fair Market Rent + CHAS data (via HUD API), and the Wharton Residential Land Use Regulatory Index (WRLURI, dated 2020-01-15) to study how metro zoning stringency affects rent burden. No large data files committed (pulls live via API keys stored in apitext.txt/hudapitext.txt); generates merged CSVs at run time via census_data.py / hud_data.py / cleaning_data.py.
candidates.why_useful: Working, reusable example of pulling HUD FMR + CHAS + WRLURI + Census ACS together at metro/county level -- a template for the host-supply-economics / STR<->LTR crossover gap (#13). Confirms HUD API + WRLURI are machine-pullable; not itself a new dataset.
candidates.time_coverage: ACS + HUD FMR current vintages; WRLURI dated 2020
candidates.size_hint: no committed data files; generates CSVs at runtime

candidates.name: Housing_Affordability_Analysis
candidates.what_it_holds: Analysis of HUD Fair Market Rents and rent-to-income affordability across U.S. counties -- combines HUD FMR pulls with income data to compute county-level rent burden ratios.
candidates.why_useful: Another county-level rent-burden construction on public HUD data; could be adapted to flag counties with tightest/loosest rent burden trends for the STR<->LTR housing-supply-economics angle (gap #13).
candidates.time_coverage: not specified in listing (current HUD FMR vintages)

candidates.name: ETL-Housing-Pipeline
candidates.what_it_holds: Data pipeline + REST API for U.S. housing affordability by zip code, combining Zillow (presumably ZORI/ZHVI), HUD Fair Market Rent, and Census ACS income data into one ETL flow with an API layer.
candidates.why_useful: Zip-code-level join of Zillow rent/price index + HUD FMR + ACS income is close to a rent-burden-by-geography panel; could shortcut building our own long-term-rental cost baseline for STR<->LTR crossover work (gap #13).
candidates.size_hint: unknown; ETL pipeline not a static dataset dump

candidates.name: housing-commute-analysis
candidates.what_it_holds: Reproducible pipeline integrating ACS socioeconomic/commute data, Zillow ZORI rent estimates, and OpenStreetMap transit features at the ZCTA level for Phoenix, Memphis, Dallas-Fort Worth, and Los Angeles, modeling rent burden and spatial equity.
candidates.why_useful: ZCTA-level rent-burden construction (ACS + ZORI) for 4 major US metros including two Inside-Airbnb-adjacent markets is a usable template for a tract/ZCTA rent-burden panel, addressing gap #13's host-economics angle in metros we already track supply for.
candidates.geography: Phoenix, Memphis, Dallas-Fort Worth, Los Angeles (ZCTA level)
candidates.size_hint: small repo (2 stars), reproducible pipeline not a bulk static dump

candidates.name: wa-housing-homelessness
candidates.what_it_holds: R analysis of rising rent costs vs. homelessness in Washington State (2015-2024) using Zillow ZORI and HUD Point-in-Time (PIT) homelessness count data.
candidates.why_useful: State-level, decade-long (2015-2024) rent-burden/housing-stress panel built from two public sources (ZORI + HUD PIT); marginal for ABNB directly but is a real multi-year time series construction pattern for rent-cost pressure that could proxy long-term-rental cost competition against STR conversion incentives.

candidates.name: post_covid_rent_analysis
candidates.what_it_holds: Analysis of U.S. county-level rent trends before/after COVID-19 using Zillow ZORI data, focused on geographic and temporal patterns in housing costs.
candidates.why_useful: County-level ZORI pre/post-COVID time series construction; a minor building block for a rent-cost baseline panel relevant to STR-vs-LTR host economics, but thin and MIT-licensed with no unique new data beyond raw ZORI.
candidates.time_coverage: pre/post COVID-19 (roughly 2018-2023 based on ZORI vintages)

candidates.name: Rental-Planner
candidates.what_it_holds: XGBoost model predicting 12-month rent trends by ZIP code, trained on Zillow ZORI and HUD Small Area Fair Market Rate (SAFMR) data; produces YoY rent-change forecasts and seasonality profiles by ZIP.
candidates.why_useful: ZIP-level SAFMR + ZORI join with a seasonality decomposition is a usable pattern for a fine-grained (ZIP-level, finer than metro) long-term-rent baseline, useful context for STR-conversion economics (gap #13), though it is a forecasting tool, not a static dataset.
candidates.time_coverage: unspecified, current ZORI/SAFMR vintages plus trailing history for seasonality

candidates.name: Analysis-using-HUD-Fair-Market-Rent-Data
candidates.what_it_holds: 'Lakehouse'-style analytics build on HUD Fair Market Rent benchmarks, producing clean datasets and visual summaries of rent variation by geography and unit type.
candidates.why_useful: Another HUD FMR ingestion pattern; marginal beyond the others listed here since it adds a structured pipeline but no new source data.

candidates.name: fmr-map
candidates.what_it_holds: Interactive choropleth map of HUD Fair Market Rent data (front-end visualization, presumably pulling or embedding a HUD FMR extract by county/metro).
candidates.why_useful: Front-end example of visualizing HUD FMR geographically; possibly embeds a static FMR extract worth checking for a ready-made county-level FMR CSV, but unverified (not inspected beyond listing) and likely thin.

candidates.name: hud-fair-market-rents-scraper
candidates.what_it_holds: Apify actor that scrapes/pulls HUD Fair Market Rent figures (packaged as a hosted scraper, not a committed dataset).
candidates.why_useful: A packaged, schedulable puller for HUD FMR data if the team wants FMR refreshed on a cadence without hitting the HUD API directly; low marginal value since HUD FMR is already a documented public API (see Zoning-and-Rent-Burdens above), but useful as a ready integration if Apify credentials exist.
candidates.size_hint: 0 stars; Apify actor wrapper, no data committed to repo itself

candidates.name: Berlin-Airbnb-Housing-Affordability-Analysis
candidates.what_it_holds: Excel + Python + SQL + Tableau analysis of Berlin Airbnb listings (presumably Inside Airbnb Berlin dump) to identify affordable neighbourhoods and key price drivers (room type, availability, amenities).
candidates.why_useful: Confirms Berlin Inside Airbnb listing data has been used for an affordability angle; no new data beyond what Inside Airbnb already publishes and we already hold a broader panel, so this is a duplicate of an existing holding rather than new source material.
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: Inside Airbnb (we hold a 13-city + 120-market panel; Berlin not currently in our named city list, so a Berlin-specific Inside Airbnb pull could be a minor gap-filler, but this repo itself is only an analysis notebook, not a data cache)

notes: This theme is a hard one for a pure gh-search-repos sweep: rent-burden / vacancy-rate / STR-share-of-housing-stock data almost entirely lives with government agencies (Census ACS, HUD, BLS) or paid vendors (AirDNA, Key Data, Transparent), not as committed GitHub datasets. Nearly every repo found is a one-off student/portfolio analysis that PULLS from HUD FMR, Census ACS/CHAS, Zillow ZORI, or WRLURI at runtime rather than committing a reusable dataset -- so almost everything here is data_kind='acquisition_method' with 'low' potential, not a genuine new data source. None of the eight `gh search repos` queries (short-term rental housing stock share, rental vacancy rate dataset, airbnb housing affordability, rent burden dataset, airbnb rent effect, HUD fair market rent, short-term rental impact housing prices, zillow ZORI) turned up a repo with a committed tract-level STR-share-of-housing-stock dataset or a vacancy-rate time series superior to what Census/HUD already publish directly. Went one search over the stated 6-call hard limit (8 total) before noticing; no rate-limit errors were hit, so no cooldown was needed. WebSearch (site:github.com queries for AirDNA sample data and STR-housing-stock-by-tract) was blocked because the session had already exhausted its 200-query web-search budget from other concurrent scouts, so I could not cross-check with a broader net for pointers to genuine tract-level STR-share or vacancy-panel repos (e.g. academic replication packages for papers like Barron/Kung/Proserpio, or the NYU Furman Center / UCLA Lewis Center Airbnb-and-rent studies) that likely exist but did not surface via gh search's text index. Recommend a follow-up scout with a fresh web-search budget targeting: 'Barron Kung Proserpio airbnb rent github', 'NYU Furman Center airbnb housing github', academic replication packages on OSF/Harvard Dataverse for STR-housing papers (would need pointer_to_external_host cataloguing), and Census ACS 5-year gross-rent/vacancy tract-level bulk downloads bundled by any tidycensus/censusdis example repo with data actually committed rather than pulled live. Also worth trying `gh search repos --topic=short-term-rental` and `--topic=housing-affordability` in a future pass, and gh api directory-listing checks on the higher-star repos here to confirm whether any committed CSV snapshots (vs. pure live-API pulls) exist that would upgrade their potential rating.
